title: RWB-S8-E7004-APP: the X4 slice has no plan row for its five consumed contracts, its rule kit, its ACE read, its outbox and inbox, its Aric route or its state vocabulary, and its legacy success criterion is owned by the harness
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.7, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E7004-APP; context pack S8 rwb-deviation (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 8 and 13); legacy RWB-E7-004; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A1.4, A2.13 and Requirements served; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.3, T6 and T-A; API Specification v4, DeviationRequest, DeviationOutcome and Deviation; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-08 and R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22; Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-06 and EV-07; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, FEAT-DVF-04 and INT-31
description: (1) The plan gives H = RWB-S8-E7004-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the story reads the rwb-case case and timers, answers the case move, reads the rwb-decision package and decision log and publishes two events, so five consumed rows and one consumed event have no plan row. (2) DP-04 is absent although the step evaluates the DEVIATIONS route set of 22 rules over 9 states and the UNIVERSAL package of 50 rules. (3) DP-05 is absent although the slice touches case and timer facts that only their owners may hold. (4) DP-09 is absent although the service owns topic rwb.deviation.events.v1 with EV-06 and EV-07 and consumes a case event. (5) The legacy FSD names the integration point Aric, INT-31 is 'Not available today; by the fraud investigator', the referral is FEAT-ADM-13 in P4, and DP-16 would add RWB-P2-E1007-CON, so the referral is out of scope and no external row exists. (6) No list of values is published for the deviation state, so the state names of TSD S8 T4 are rule facts and R-DEV-21 has no message ID. (7) The R-DEV-20 service level, the escalation of R-DEV-20 and the unmapped code of R-DEV-21 carry no message ID in any source. (8) The map publishes two operations only, so the assignment of R-DEV-04 is the rule's inside the raise and no operation re-assigns a deviation by hand. (9) The spawned slice owns only legacy AC2, while AC1 is owned by RWB-ITG-E7004-ITG, so the success path of this story is proved by the harness and by the four legacy Component cases and by no criterion of its own. (10) EP07 maps to wave 4 while the service is wave 2 in Arch v5, and the plan gives wave 4, so the plan value is kept and no W-MAP conflict is raised.
evidence: split plan slice RWB-S8-E7004-APP with three H rows and empty C, I and X; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 DP-04, DP-05, DP-09 and DP-16, R5.6 and R5.7; context pack ownership rows (table deviation, 2 REST operations, events EV-06 and EV-07, 0 jobs, workflow DeviationWorkflow), service row (wave 2) and connection-matrix row S8 (Temporal and events to P3, REST and events to P1, Temporal and events to P10); Temporal and Drools slides 8 and 13 (DeviationWorkflow, pause of the stage clock, prescription clock keeps running); TSD S8 T3.2 lists and T4 state machine; T-A.2 idempotency of the patch 'Not applicable'; API Specification v4, DeviationOutcome body with outcome and note only; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, INT-31 and FEAT-ADM-13; FSD S8 A2.13.3.1; legacy RWB-E7-004 Acceptance criteria, Data, Endpoints and Guardrails
area: Dependency, ownership, data, vocabulary and requirement trace
proposed: Keep the plan's H, C, I and X rows as they stand; record the two rwb-case rows, the boundary signal and the two rwb-decision rows as class C in fact with their placeholders; record RWB-PLT-E1072-CON with RWB-P7-E1073-CON as the rule kit, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON as the outbox and inbox library and RWB-PLT-E1037-CON with RWB-P4-E1037-CON as the access guard; keep the Aric referral with FEAT-ADM-13 in P4 and raise no external row; publish a list of values for the deviation state before the DB story; bind the escalation and the unmapped code to a message or record them as message-free; confirm the ownership of legacy AC1 with the harness and let the four Component cases cover the build; keep EP07 at wave 4 and record the service wave 2 as no conflict

title: RWB-S8-E7004-CON: the consumed operation names, the boundary signal, the event names, the state vocabulary and the patch idempotency of rwb-deviation have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E7004-CON; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; legacy RWB-E7-004; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.13.2, A2.13.3.1, A2.13.4.3 and Screens; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2 and T-A.1 and T-A.2; API Specification v4, DeviationRequest, DeviationOutcome and Deviation; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-08 and R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22; Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-06 and EV-07; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, INT-31
description: (1) The rwb-case and rwb-decision rows name no operation, so five consumed rows carry a placeholder. (2) No source publishes a REST path or an operation that pauses or resumes a stage clock on behalf of a stage, and the S8 row of the connection matrix shows Temporal to P3 rather than a REST call, so the pause and resume are declared on the workflow boundary. (3) TSD S8 T3.2 publishes three lists and no list of values for the deviation state, so no enumeration can be declared for a state and the vocabulary gap is carried. (4) The target event names of EV-06 and EV-07 are not published in any catalogue; only the naming rule of Template and Rules R4 gives their form, and the same holds for the consumed case event. (5) TSD S8 T-A.2 gives error sets as status codes with no message ID per condition, so each condition is bound to a message of the legacy and FSD set. (6) TSD S8 T-A.2 declares the patch idempotency 'Not applicable' while the published body of DeviationOutcome carries only outcome and note and the wave 4 harness drives one Idempotency-Key per patch, so the baseline follows the TSD and describes a repeated outcome as 409. (7) The map publishes two operations only, so no clear operation, no GET /deviations and no assignment operation exists, and a manual re-assignment has no published surface. (8) No Aric operation exists and INT-31 is 'Not available today', so no external call can be declared and the referral stays with FEAT-ADM-13 in P4. (9) The plan's C, I and X rows of this slice are empty while the contract declares five consumed rows and one consumed event.
evidence: TSD S8 T-A.1 operations API-S8-001 and API-S8-002, T-A.2 error lists of 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 without message ids and the patch idempotency row 'Not applicable', T3.1 field list and T3.2 three lists; API Specification v4, Deviation (required list and three enumerations), DeviationRequest (deviationCode, reason, documentIds) and DeviationOutcome (outcome, note); context pack ownership rows (table deviation, 2 REST operations, 2 events, 0 jobs) and connection-matrix row S8; Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-06 and EV-07; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, INT-31 and FEAT-ADM-13; legacy RWB-E7-004 messages MSG-S8-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003
area: Contract surface, interface names, vocabulary and idempotency
proposed: Publish the baseline with the placeholders, bind every error condition to one message ID of section 14, declare the case boundary as the child workflow's input, signals and stage outcome, declare the two events on the naming rule's names and confirm them with rwb-comms and rwb-treatment, settle the deviation state vocabulary with the data owners before the DB story, settle the patch idempotency between the TSD and the harness before the tag, and record the tag date in the contract README
